block.heading: How to read these case results
paragraphs: These anonymised case studies show what we changed and how each property's results compared before and after our work began. Each result states its comparison period: either the same six months a year earlier or a later month against the month before takeover. Owner workload figures compare weekly averages.

Before you sign, we also share anonymised revenue per available room (RevPAR), occupancy and net operating income (NOI) figures comparing the 12 months before we took over with the 12 months after. We can arrange calls with up to three current owner clients who have agreed to act as references.

block.heading: Motel Information Technology, Tailored to the Way You Work
paragraphs: You'll have a dedicated IT representative who gets to know how your motel runs and helps you choose the technologies that suit it. We don't hand you a standard package. We build your motel information technology around what you need.

items.heading: Operations Management
paragraphs: Keep daily motel work aligned with your goals through our [remote operations service](/operations-management/). We oversee improvements, support your staff and reduce purchasing costs, with help preparing new properties to open.

items.heading: Revenue Management
paragraphs: Hand off room pricing with our [remote revenue management service](/revenue-management/). We adjust rates each business day, turn expected demand into financial targets and manage distribution around your property’s needs and existing systems.

items.heading: Information Technology
paragraphs: Whether you need a system change or ongoing help, our [motel IT service](/information-technology/) supports the way you work. We select and deploy technology, protect access and data, and keep systems updated.

block.heading: Ownership-Aligned Business Plans and Hands-On Oversight

items.heading: Ownership-led planning
paragraphs: Your return targets drive our budget, staffing and capital decisions, not last year's budget. If a target is unrealistic for your market, we flag it during planning because it requires early reforecasting.

items.heading: Whole-property coverage
paragraphs: We provide operations management for motels and hotels remotely. That covers budgets, pricing, staffing, costs, contracts and reporting. We have no staff on site, so your teams deliver the on-site services.

items.heading: Local management contact
paragraphs: If you don't have a resident GM, we handle planning, pricing, budgets, vendors and staff leadership through the on-site lead you nominate. If your property has more than 50 rooms or has food and beverage outlets, we recommend an on-site duty manager on every shift.

items.heading: Evidence before signing
paragraphs: Before you sign, our [case studies and owner references](/case-studies/) give you calls with up to 3 current clients who have consented to speak with you. You also get anonymised RevPAR, occupancy and NOI comparisons covering the 12 months before and the 12 months after we took over.

items.heading: Existing agreement restrictions
paragraphs: We keep your SOPs and brand standards, support your department heads and follow your franchise, loan, lease and supply restrictions. Our onboarding review identifies any savings or changes those terms block, and you decide whether to keep or renegotiate those terms.

items.heading: Your business plan
paragraphs: Your plan includes a 12-month budget, a staffing model, revenue, GOP and NOI targets and a 5-year capital plan. We base it on the last 24 months of your P&L and bookings, on market and competitive-set data and on your return targets.

items.heading: Delivery and review
paragraphs: We deliver your plan within 20 business days of receiving your data and read-only system access. We review actual results with you on monthly strategy calls. When results diverge from the plan, we update forecasts quarterly, and we rebuild the plan every year.

items.heading: Coaching and operating procedures
paragraphs: We coach your commercial team as they make live decisions. We also work with your revenue-generating departments to set best practices and standard operating procedures, so those practices carry on after we step back.

items.heading: Commercial technology support
paragraphs: Our [technology service](/information-technology/) covers assessment, selection, installation and configuration. It also includes training your staff on your systems, marketing applications and programs.

items.question: Can I hire you just for HR or recruitment without handing over management of the motel, and what scope options do you offer?
items.answer: Yes, we provide HR services on their own or as part of full management, and you buy only the modules you need. Full HR planning, executive search, recruitment, payroll, and consulting and policy projects are each available on their own; only ongoing leadership of your property team requires full management.

items.question: Who remains the legal employer, and which hiring, pay and dismissal decisions remain with the owner?
items.answer: Your ownership entity stays the legal employer, and pay scales, yearly wage rises, bonuses and dismissals stay under your final control. Within the budget you approve, we set hourly rates and propose disciplinary measures, but any salary or senior appointment outside that budget needs your approval, and nobody is terminated until you or the manager you nominate signs off.

items.question: How do you recruit for my motel remotely, how long does it take to fill a role, and do I approve each hire?
items.answer: We recruit, place and onboard candidates remotely and interview them by video, while your named local contact checks original identity and right-to-work documents in person. From the start of the search, hourly roles take 14 to 21 days to fill and management roles take 30 to 45 days. Within the agreed budget, we hire with your general manager, unless you want to approve hires yourself.

items.question: How is HR charged — per employee, per hire, per property — and is it included in the management fee?
items.answer: If we manage your motel, staff leadership, recruitment and payroll processing are covered by your management fee. For standalone recruitment you pay per hire, and for HR consulting or policy work you pay a fixed project fee. We quote before you sign, based on your headcount, the hires you expect each year, the modules you select and how many properties you have.

items.question: Is your HR service worth it for a 20-room motel with five staff, or is it for larger hotels?
items.answer: There's no minimum headcount, so a 20-room motel with five staff is eligible. For a small property, we concentrate on recruitment, onboarding, payroll and employment compliance, and leave out programmes designed only for larger hotels.

items.question: What can I check with the weekly rate-review template?
items.answer: It's a worksheet for checking booking pace, availability, local demand and proposed rate changes.

block.heading: Data-Driven Assessment of Your Current Operations
paragraphs: We assess how your property runs today using benchmarking, reporting and technology for upgrading your systems.

steps.heading: Share operating records
steps.text: You give us read-only access to 12 months of P&L statements, PMS reports, payroll and timekeeping records, maintenance and work-order logs, and guest reviews and complaint logs, along with your current vendor contracts.

steps.heading: Rebuild missing baselines
steps.text: If your labour, maintenance or guest-service records are incomplete, the assessment still goes ahead. We rebuild baselines from payroll exports, vendor invoices and online reviews. We mark the less precise findings as estimates that show direction, not exact figures.

steps.heading: Assessment fee
steps.text: You pay a fixed assessment fee. It rises with your room count, your revenue outlets and the number of systems we connect beyond your PMS and channel manager. Rebuilding missing records also raises the fee.

steps.heading: Extra scope
steps.text: Analysing more than 3 years of history costs more, and so does reviewing several properties together. If your hotel has more than 200 rooms, you get a custom quote.

steps.heading: Establish complete tracking
steps.text: We don't hold back the assessment until your records are perfect. Instead, we set up tracking while we diagnose, which gives you 90 days of complete data for the follow-up review.

steps.heading: Identify recovery priorities
steps.text: Our recovery diagnosis examines your financial health, market position, physical condition and operating performance. We trace revenue, cost, staffing and brand-compliance problems to their causes. Then we define corrections and repositioning opportunities specific to your property.

items.heading: Advance billing and payment
items.text: Monthly fees are invoiced in advance at the start of each month, and payment is due within 15 days by ACH, international wire or credit card. Our prices are in USD, though you can pay in CAD, EUR or AUD at the exchange rate on the invoice date. A full management agreement also carries a one-time onboarding fee, separate from the revenue management setup fee.

items.heading: Included and third-party costs
items.text: Your fee pays for our team's time and our own pricing, reporting and BI tools. Third-party costs are billed to your property at cost, with no mark-up from us. These include your PMS, channel manager, other software subscriptions, OTA commissions, photographers and specialist partners.

items.heading: Taxes and transfer charges
items.text: USD prices don't include applicable sales taxes, and we add those only where the law requires it for your property's location. Your bank's transfer charges are yours to pay. Currency-conversion costs for payments in CAD, EUR or AUD are on us.

items.heading: Ending a plan
items.text: Each service's minimum term is set out in its proposal. Once that term is over, you can end your plan with 30 days' written notice, and there's no exit fee. The one-time setup fee can't be refunded after setup work starts, and we don't refund fees already paid for the current month.

items.heading: Pausing a plan
items.text: After the minimum term, you can also pause, again with 30 days' written notice. Monthly billing then stops for up to three months. You won't pay a pause fee, and if you restart within that time, you won't pay a new setup fee either.

items.heading: Changing plans
items.text: Upgrades take effect on the day you make the change, and the price difference is prorated for the rest of that month. Downgrades start from your next billing cycle.

items.heading: Results and refunds
items.text: Revenue results aren't guaranteed, and we don't offer refunds, because market demand, competitors and other outside factors all affect performance. What we do is work closely with you, check results against agreed targets on every monthly strategy call and change the strategy whenever a target is missed.

block.heading: Three properties: challenges, actions and results

items.heading: 32-room motel in Oregon, United States
paragraphs: Revenue management. Rates stayed the same most weeks, making quiet weekdays hard to fill and leaving busy weekends priced too low. We reviewed booking pace, historical occupancy and local demand remotely, introduced daily rates by room type and arrival date, adjusted minimum stays around busy weekends, and sent weekly performance summaries and pricing priorities. Over the first six months compared with the same six months a year earlier, occupancy rose from 58% to 69%, average daily rate increased 9%, and revenue per available room increased 30%.

items.heading: 46-room hotel in Ontario, Canada
paragraphs: OTA management. Inconsistent room descriptions and unclear cancellation terms on Booking.com and Expedia left the owner spending hours correcting availability and answering avoidable questions. We corrected listing details, amenities and policies, reorganised owner-supplied photos, aligned room mapping and availability, monitored listing performance, and handled OTA-related guest messages remotely. In month four compared with the month before takeover, Booking.com listing conversion rose from 2.1% to 2.8% and Expedia listing conversion rose from 1.8% to 2.3%. The owner's OTA administration fell from eight to two hours per week, comparing the weekly average in month four with the month before takeover.

items.heading: 28-room motel in Queensland, Australia
paragraphs: Full remote management. The owner handled guest messages, pricing and maintenance coordination without consistent handovers, leading to slow replies and missed follow-ups. We took over reservations, guest messaging and arrival instructions remotely, coordinated cleaning and maintenance with local contractors carrying out all on-site work, managed pricing and OTA availability through a shared operating calendar, and introduced weekly owner reports covering performance, outstanding issues and approval requests. In month six compared with the month before takeover, median guest-message response time fell from three hours to 24 minutes, and maintenance requests resolved within 48 hours rose from 54% to 87%. The owner's routine operational workload fell from 26 to six hours per week, comparing the weekly average in month six with the month before takeover.

block.heading: Tax Filings, Privacy and Payment Compliance
paragraphs: We process and report your lodging, occupancy, sales and use taxes by each local deadline. Licensed local tax partners submit your returns, payroll filings and other statutory filings, and we oversee their work. Your own accountant keeps your corporate income tax returns, statutory financial statement audits and any filings that need their locally licensed signature. We supply the supporting schedules for that work. Each month we also export your ledger to QuickBooks, so your accountant can keep using it for year-end and tax work.

Our [privacy and payment safeguards](/privacy-policy/) follow Canada's PIPEDA, the GDPR for French properties, the Australian Privacy Act and relevant US state laws. Card data stays outside our systems because we use PCI DSS-compliant processors. We provide Canadian cloud hosting, and on request we store data for French properties in the EU.

block.heading: Project Timelines, Budgets & Monthly Cost Reporting
rows: PIP timeline
4 to 8 months from appointment to closeout. About 2 to 3 months of that is pre-construction.
Full renovation timeline
9 to 15 months, of which 3 to 5 months is pre-construction.
New-build timeline
18 to 30 months, of which 6 to 12 months is pre-construction.
Pre-construction
These periods include design, permits, pricing and procurement.
Total project budget
Your budget covers hard construction costs; architect, engineer and consultant fees; permits and connections; FF&E, OS&E and IT; pre-opening costs; and construction-period financing.
Contingency
We set aside 10% of hard costs for new builds and 15% for renovations at operating motels. No draw happens without your prior written approval.
Budget and schedule
We give you both at appointment and track performance against them throughout. When a budget line is forecast to exceed its allowance by more than 5%, we flag it for your approval.
Monthly reporting

You get a written cost report, a dashboard and a monthly owner report. Together they show approved budgets, signed-contract and purchase-order commitments, actual spending, forecast cost to complete and the funding still required. You can also view the dashboard live.
Cost accountability
We track committed, forecast and contingency costs by budget line, programme and property, and we link every cost change to the decision behind it.
Progress reporting
Our reports cover schedule progress, critical-path milestones, open risks and every approved or pending scope change. Between monthly reports, we send you a short weekly progress email.
Closeout documents
You receive PDFs of the as-built drawings, operation and maintenance manuals, warranties, guarantees, contractor final releases, final cost reconciliation and the completed punch list.
